info.title: Kantel API
info.description: Kantel's public API for host apps, such as Lleverage, and for Kantel's own console, which uses it like any other client.

post.description: A link for an iframe: a watch-only live view of one of the session's open browsers, or a replay of one, open or closed. Needs viewer on the session; never an agent. The link carries a short-lived token scoped to that one view (never control), lasting `minutes`. A closed browser has no live view (`expired`); a deployment whose browsers keep no recordings has no replay (`unavailable`), and a recording past its retention is `expired`. Audited as `browser.session.embedded`, without the link.

delete.description: Deletes the calling person and their personal account: its hosts are removed, every API key that acts for them is revoked, they leave every organisation, and their sign-ins end. Their private sandboxes in an organisation stay, stopped, as when they leave it. `conflict` while their personal account has sandboxes, saved snapshots or bundles, or while they are an organisation's last owner. Once accepted, it carries on in the background until everything has gone. People only, and not a deployment super-admin.

post.description: Makes a sandbox and starts it: an isolate unless `type` says `microvm`, from a snapshot when `from` names one. `resources` sets its vCPUs and memory, and a microVM's disk (`diskGb`), which may also go alone or beside `size` (`getSandboxShapes` says what may be asked); `size`, a named size, still works for now. Answers as soon as it is placed (`starting`), or once it runs with `wait`. A full deployment is `exhausted`; no host able to run the type is `unavailable`. `mounts` (experimental) are for microVMs only: an isolate's are refused (`not_supported`), because an isolate is a shell over files the host keeps, with no file system of its own to mount a drive or a bucket into. A mount whose bundle or bucket source isn't the account's is `not_found`; with the deployment's `KANTEL_MOUNTS` switch off, any `mounts` are `not_supported`. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

post.summary: Upgrade an isolate to a microVM
post.description: Turns a running or stopped isolate into a microVM with the same ID, name, labels, env, environments, egress grants and protected variables. Its `/workspace` files are put in the microVM at `/home/user/workspace`, and `/workspace` there is a link to them, so paths an agent used keep working. A stopped isolate comes back as a running microVM. Upgrade when a command answers `needsMicrovm`, or before work an isolate can't do (`git`, Node or Python packages, a build, Docker). Answers once the microVM runs (unless `wait` is `false`), and a microVM is answered as it is. If the microVM can't be made, the call fails and the isolate is left as it was. Commands and file calls made meanwhile wait for it. Its isolate time ends and its microVM time starts at the upgrade; a `sandbox.upgraded` event records it. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

post.summary: Restart a sandbox on the latest base
post.description: Restarts the machine on the newest base image, on its disk as it is: a running sandbox's disk is saved and it is stopped first (as `stop` does, without its memory), then it boots cold on the latest base. Memory is lost, and so are running programs. A running sandbox is never patched underneath: this is how an outdated one (`base.outdated`) moves on. Answers once it is starting. A sandbox starting, stopping or being deleted is `conflict`; one another call moves after this restart has stopped it is `aborted`. A key needs `sandboxes:write`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned image patching on (`KANTEL_IMAGE_PATCHING`).

post.summary: Get an upload URL for a file
post.description: A short-lived URL on the API, streamed straight to the sandbox's host: `PUT` the file to it as the raw request body, of any size, with no `Authorization` header; the answer is `{ path, size }`. Missing directories are made, and a file already there is replaced only once the upload is complete. The URL is bound to this sandbox and path, and expires after `ttlSeconds`. A path in a read-only mount is refused (`conflict`). The sandbox must be running when the URL is used. Treat it as a secret. A key needs `files`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`).

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.summary: Get a download URL for a file
post.description: A short-lived URL on the API, streamed straight from the sandbox's host: `GET` it, with no `Authorization` header, for the file's bytes as they are when it is fetched, whatever its size (`HEAD` for its size alone). The URL is bound to this sandbox and path, and expires after `ttlSeconds`. The sandbox must be running when the URL is used. Treat it as a secret. A key needs `files`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`).

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

put.summary: Extract an archive into a directory
put.description: Writes every file, directory and symbolic link of a tar (or a gzipped tar) into `path`, in one call. An entry whose name is absolute or climbs out of `path` (`..`), a link that points out of it, an entry under such a link, and hard links, devices and FIFOs are refused (`invalid`) before anything is written. A `path` in a read-only mount, or with one under it, is refused (`conflict`). Files are owned by the sandbox's user, with their modes from the tar. A key needs `files`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`).

oomKills.description: `sandbox.oom_kill`: how many processes its kernel killed for memory since its last reading.

environmentIds.description: `sandbox.environments_changed`: the sandbox's environments now, in order.

path.description: `sandbox.upgraded`: `host` when the isolate's own host made the microVM and moved its files, `control-plane` when the microVM went on another host and Kantel moved them.

files.description: `sandbox.upgraded`: the files, links and directories moved.

EventType.title: EventType
EventType.description: `sandbox.created`: made, before it runs. `sandbox.running`: it runs commands now, after a create, resume, fork or recovery. `sandbox.stopped`, `sandbox.paused`: it stopped (by a call, its auto-stop or its idle stop), or paused. `sandbox.error`: it entered `error`. `sandbox.degraded`, `sandbox.recovered`: its host lost and regained it; `sandbox.degraded` also when its environment's secret file or repository couldn't be set up (its reason says which), which leaves it running, and when its guest agent stops answering (its `health` `unresponsive`), with `sandbox.recovered` once it answers again. `sandbox.environments_changed`: an environment was attached to it or detached from it (`data.attached` or `data.detached`, and `data.environmentIds`, in order). `sandbox.oom_kill`: a microVM ran out of memory and its kernel killed processes (`data.oomKills` of them since its last reading); it keeps running. `sandbox.upgraded`: an isolate became a microVM with the same ID (`upgradeSandbox`, or its `autoUpgrade`): `data.from` and `data.to` the types, `data.previousState`, `data.path` (`host` when its own host made the microVM, `control-plane` when its files were moved to another host), `data.files`, `data.bytes` and `data.durationMs`. `sandbox.deleted`: erased. `snapshot.saved`, `snapshot.deleted`: a saved snapshot was made or deleted.

url.description: Its HTTPS URL. Unless `public`, the answer to exposing it carries a token anyone holding it may use, shown only then (Kantel keeps its hash); listed, the URL has none. Exposing the port again gives a new token and ends the old. Access through it ends when the key or sign-in that exposed it loses access to the sandbox.

public.description: Anyone with the URL may open it, with no token. Default false.

path.description: The absolute directory it was extracted into.

content.description: The file, or with `offset` or `length`, the part read.

size.description: The whole file's size in bytes.

offset.description: With `offset` or `length`: the byte `content` starts at. At `size`, it's empty.

FileContent.title: FileContent
FileContent.description: A file of at most 1 MiB, or a part of at most 1 MiB of a larger one, read with `offset` and `length`.

url.description: The signed URL. Send the request straight to it, with no `Authorization` header. Treat it as a secret until it expires.

method.description: `GET` downloads the file. `PUT` uploads the request's raw body as the file.

path.description: The absolute path the URL is bound to.

FileUrl.title: FileUrl
FileUrl.description: A short-lived URL for one file of one sandbox, streamed to or from the sandbox's host, so a file of any size moves without base64.

path.description: An absolute path, or one relative to a microVM's `/home/user` or an isolate's `/workspace`.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the URL may be used: default 900 (15 minutes), at most 3600.

snapshotId.description: Fork from this snapshot of the sandbox. Default: its newest, or its live state.

injected.description: Kantel put its guest agent into the image at boot (any Linux image), rather than the image shipping it.

arch.description: The machine, as `uname -m` says it: `x86_64` or `aarch64`.

libc.description: The image's C library; `none` for a static userland such as busybox's.

shell.description: The shell a `command` runs in, such as `/bin/bash`; absent: `argv` only.

init.description: PID 1: the image's systemd, or Kantel's own init when the image has none.

GuestCapabilities.title: GuestCapabilities
GuestCapabilities.description: What a microVM's image has, as its guest agent found it when it last started: its OS, and whether it has a desktop, a browser (and `browserSurface`, the browser alone on a display of its own) and Docker.

detail.description: What the guest agent found, such as `Xtigervnc, Openbox, Selkies`.

reason.description: Why it isn't available, in words, such as `No desktop in this image`.

kvm.description: `/dev/kvm` opens inside, so containers and VMs in it can nest.

detail.description: What the guest agent found, such as `Xtigervnc, Openbox, Selkies`.

reason.description: Why it isn't available, in words, such as `No desktop in this image`.

GuestFeature.title: GuestFeature
GuestFeature.description: One thing a microVM's image has or lacks.

oomKills.description: How many processes its kernel has killed for memory since it booted (its `oom_kill`). It grows until the VM boots again: a stop and start, or a recovery.

pressureSome.description: The share of the last 10 seconds in which at least one of its tasks was stalled waiting for memory (its kernel's memory pressure, `some` avg10).

pressureFull.description: The share of the last 10 seconds in which every task that wanted to run was stalled waiting for memory (`full` avg10). Near 1, the machine does little but reclaim memory and stops answering.

GuestMemory.title: GuestMemory
GuestMemory.description: A microVM's newest memory figures from inside its guest, as of `at`: each absent where its guest's agent doesn't send it (an image from before them) or its kernel has none.

name.description: Its pretty name, such as `Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)`.

latestVersion.description: The version hosts should run: the deployment's `KANTEL_HOST_VERSION` when it sets one, otherwise Kantel's latest release. Absent when neither is known.

updateAvailable.description: True when it runs an older version than `latestVersion` (any other, when the deployment sets `KANTEL_HOST_VERSION`), so it can be updated. Absent otherwise.

accountId.description: The account the host belongs to, when it was added to one by its people: only that account's sandboxes run on it. Absent for a host the deployment's super-admin joined, which any account's sandboxes may use.

savedSnapshotBytesLimit.description: The most bytes of saved snapshots each account may keep on this host. Each saved snapshot counts at its full size, the files it shares with other snapshots included, so copies that share files count separately. A save past it answers `exhausted`. Absent: no limit.

Host.title: Host
Host.description: A machine that runs sandboxes. It dials out to the control plane; it takes no inbound ports.

totalBytes.description: The size of the filesystem that holds the host's files.

usedBytes.description: What is used on it, by anything.

savedSnapshotsBytes.description: Saved snapshots: of the snapshot files counted here, those every account's saved snapshots on the host hold, each file once.

automaticSnapshotsBytes.description: The rest of the host's snapshots: automatic ones, and any Kantel has no record of.

sandboxesBytes.description: Sandboxes' own disks, and their memory while they're stopped.

imagesBytes.description: Base images: the guest kernel and root filesystems, and templates' root filesystems.

templatesBytes.description: Template snapshots, which new sandboxes start from.

bundlesBytes.description: The cache of bundle images that sandboxes mount.

otherBytes.description: The rest of the used space: the operating system, logs and other programs.

HostDiskUsage.title: HostDiskUsage
HostDiskUsage.description: What takes the space on a host's disk, as the host measured it last (every few minutes), counting only files on the filesystem that holds the host's files. Each file counts once, in the first of these it is in: bundles, images, templates, sandboxes, snapshots. Memory a stop's snapshot shares with its sandbox counts for the sandbox. Snapshots are split into saved and automatic by Kantel's own records, not by the host.

token.description: `kth_…`, shown once. It joins one host.

command.description: The one-line command that installs and registers a host with it.

mode.description: How the host admits microVMs' memory. `reserved`: by what they were given, up to `maxRatio` times `capacityMiB`. `used` (memory over-commit, experimental): by `committedMiB`, what they use and may soon use, within what the machine has available and up to `maxRatio` times `capacityMiB` given.

state.description: How short of memory the host is. `tight`: it reclaims guests' page cache. `refusing`: it refuses new sandboxes. `critical`: it ends the largest process in the guest holding the most memory.

totalMiB.description: The machine's memory, or the limit of the control group kantel-host runs in.

reserveMiB.description: What is kept for the host's own processes and never given to sandboxes.

reservedMiB.description: What the host's sandboxes were given.

committedMiB.description: What its microVMs count for: each its peak of the last minutes plus headroom, at most its size.

guestUsedMiB.description: What its microVMs' guests say they use, page cache aside.

residentMiB.description: What its microVMs hold of the machine's memory, their guests' page cache included.

availableMiB.description: What the machine has available now (MemAvailable).

swapUsedMiB.description: Swap in use on the machine.

pressureSome.description: Memory pressure: the share of the last 10 seconds some task waited on memory.

pressureFull.description: The share of the last 10 seconds every task waited on memory.

maxRatio.description: The most sandboxes may be given, as a multiple of `capacityMiB`.

HostMemory.title: HostMemory
HostMemory.description: A host's memory, in MiB, as it last reported it (every heartbeat).

checked.description: True when this call read Kantel's latest release again. False when another check was made in the last 30 seconds, whose answer stands: nothing more was read.

latestVersion.description: The latest kantel-host release now known, which hosts' `latestVersion` and `updateAvailable` follow. Absent when none has been read.

HostState.title: HostState
HostState.description: `online`: connected and taking sandboxes. `unreachable`: its connection dropped; its sandboxes can't be reached until it is back. `draining`: connected, but takes no new sandboxes. `revoked`: its credential is revoked.

HostUpdate.title: HostUpdate
HostUpdate.description: An update asked for in the last 10 minutes that the host hasn't connected on yet. Absent once it has, or after 10 minutes, when it didn't take.

intervalMs.description: How far apart the points are: 5000 from a current host.

memTotalBytes.description: 0 until the host has sent a reading.

diskTotalBytes.description: 0 until the host has sent a reading.

points.description: Oldest first, at most the last hour; with `since`, only those after it. Empty for a host that doesn't send its readings yet (an older kantel-host).

HostUsage.title: HostUsage
HostUsage.description: A host's readings as they came, for a live graph: poll with `since` set to the last point's `at` for only the newer ones.

cpu.description: CPU utilisation over the interval ending at `at`, 0 to 1 of all the host's CPUs.

code.description: The join code, such as `kji_…`. Shown once, when the invite is made.

emailed.description: Only when the invite is made: whether Kantel emailed it, with a link that joins with its code. False without an email, where the deployment sends no mail, or when the send failed.

Invite.title: Invite
Invite.description: A way into an organisation: whoever joins with its code becomes a member.

enforced.description: Whether an isolate's memory is a hard limit (its heap, ArrayBuffers and WebAssembly memory together): true when every host the account's isolates may run on says its isolate runtime enforces it. Otherwise the runtime records it, and the account VM's memory, shared by its isolates, is the limit.

secret.description: The key itself, `ksk_…`. Shown once: store it now.
The token itself, `kpt_…`. Shown once: store it now.

LiveFrame.title: LiveFrame
LiveFrame.description: One frame of the account's live stream.

LiveHello.title: LiveHello
LiveHello.description: The stream is open. Read what you show again after each one: changes made while no stream was open (before the first, between a drop and the reconnection) are not sent.

LiveSandboxChange.title: LiveSandboxChange
LiveSandboxChange.description: A sandbox moved to `state`, whoever moved it (a call from the console, the CLI, the API or an SDK, its auto-stop, its host). No `previousState`: it was just made. Read the sandbox for the rest.

MemberRole.title: MemberRole
MemberRole.description: `member`: uses the organisation's shared sandboxes and snapshots and makes their own. `admin`: also manages members, API keys, webhooks, telemetry and the proxy. `owner`: also renames or deletes the organisation. A personal account's person is its `owner`.

memoryMbPerVcpu.description: Memory follows vCPUs: each vCPU has at least `min` and at most `max` MB.

presets.description: Each shape a host makes by name. Hosts may give one name different shapes: each is its own entry.

custom.description: Whether a host takes shapes off the presets; when false, only the presets. Unless a create asks for a disk (`diskGb`), its host gives one; the sandbox's `resources` say what it got.

MicrovmShapes.title: MicrovmShapes
MicrovmShapes.description: Absent when no host the account may use runs microVMs. `diskGb` is the disk a microVM may ask for (`resources.diskGb`), whatever its vCPUs and memory: within the hosts' limits and the free disk they last reported, its `default` the default preset's. A sandbox no host has the free disk for now goes to `error` with `placementReason` `insufficient_capacity`. `diskGb` is absent when no host takes a disk off its presets, or none has the free disk for its least.

path.description: Where it appears in the sandbox: absolute and normalised, not `/`, not at or under a system directory (`/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/lib` and the like), and not overlapping another mount.

Mount.title: Mount
Mount.description: Files from outside the sandbox, read-only inside it: nothing in the sandbox can change them.

MountStatus.title: MountStatus
MountStatus.description: `pending`: its host is still putting it in place. `ready`: its files are there. `failed`: they aren't, and `error` says why; the sandbox runs without it.

prefix.description: The secret's first characters, such as `kpt_5n2p`, to tell tokens apart.

scopes.description: At most these, on top of the person's role in each account. Absent: whatever their role allows. Never `hosts:admin`: a token doesn't act as a deployment super-admin.

accounts.description: Only these accounts. Absent: every account its person belongs to, ones they join later included.

lastUsedAt.description: When it last signed a call in, to within a minute. Absent until its first use.

PersonalToken.title: PersonalToken
PersonalToken.description: A personal access token (`kpt_…`). Its secret is never stored or shown after it is made.

PersonalTokenPolicy.title: PersonalTokenPolicy
PersonalTokenPolicy.description: Whether members' personal access tokens (`kpt_…`) may act in the organisation. `blocked`: a call made with one is `forbidden` there, and members use the console or one of the organisation's API keys. Always `allowed` in a personal account. Absent from a gateway before it: `allowed`.

PlacementReason.title: PlacementReason
PlacementReason.description: Why a sandbox couldn't be placed on a host. `no_host`: no host it may use is connected. `no_host_for_type`: none runs its type. `no_host_with_labels`: none has every label in `hostLabels`. `no_host_offers_size`: none offers its size or can make its resources. `no_host_enforces_egress`: none that could take it enforces egress grants or protected variables. `no_host_for_template`: none that could take it runs templates, or builds the template's custom image. `insufficient_capacity`: hosts match but none has the memory or disk free now; retry later. `host_unavailable`: the host its disk or snapshot is on can't take it now (offline, draining or not one it may use, or gone during the boot). `account_limit`: the account runs as many sandboxes as it may.

organisationId.description: The organisation the project is in: always the caller's.

enabled.description: Send sandboxes' outbound traffic through the proxy.

defaultAction.description: What happens to a host no rule names.

deny.description: Hosts always refused; deny wins over allow.

attribution.description: Tell the upstream which sandbox and account each request came from, in signed `Kantel-Sandbox` and `Kantel-Account` headers.

ProxySettings.title: ProxySettings
ProxySettings.description: Where sandboxes' outbound traffic may go, and through what, for one account. Experimental.

ProxySettingsExpected.title: ProxySettingsExpected
ProxySettingsExpected.description: The settings as you last read them: `GET /proxy`'s answer will do. Given, the write is refused with `conflict` if they have changed since, so an edit made from an older read can't undo someone else's: read them again and redo the edit. Left out, the settings are replaced whatever they hold.

url.description: Another proxy every allowed request goes on to, such as a Mehen.

headerNames.description: The names of the headers Kantel sends it; their values are never shown.

publicUrl.description: Where hosts reach this control plane: the address in every join command, such as `https://kantel.example.com`.

source.description: `console`: a super-admin set it here. `deployment`: the deployment's own (`KANTEL_PUBLIC_URL`, or the address the call came in at).

deploymentUrl.description: The deployment's own, which `publicUrl` goes back to when cleared.

loopback.description: `publicUrl` is a loopback address (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`): only a host on the same machine can join.

digest.description: The digest the channel publishes from now.

expected.description: The list as you last read it. Given, the write is refused with `conflict` if the list has changed since, so an edit made from an older read can't undo someone else's: read it again and redo the edit. Left out, the list is replaced whatever it holds.

The list as you last read it. Given, the write is refused with `conflict` if the list has changed since, so an edit made from an older read can't undo someone else's: read it again and redo the edit. Left out, the list is replaced whatever it holds.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.
The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

objects.description: How many objects the listing it shows holds.

listedAt.description: When the listing it shows began (ms since the epoch), after the call arrived: it has every object the bucket held then.

RefreshedMount.title: RefreshedMount
RefreshedMount.description: A bucket mount as the sandbox shows it after a refresh.

items.description: Each bucket mount refreshed, in the sandbox's order.

path.description: Just the bucket mount at this path. Default: every bucket mount of the sandbox's.

command.description: A shell command line, run with `bash -lc` (or the isolate's shell).

cwd.description: Default: a microVM's `/home/user` or an isolate's `/workspace`. A relative path starts there.

timeoutMs.description: Default 30 000; at most 600 000 (10 minutes). A detached command has no limit unless this gives one.

detached.description: Start it and answer at once; it runs with no time limit unless `timeoutMs` gives one. Read it back by its ID.

subdomain.description: Its name under the deployment's sandbox domain, which its public port URLs start with.

image.description: The base image a microVM was made from, such as `ubuntu-26.04`.

reason.description: Why it is in `error` or `degraded`, in words; or why Kantel stopped or paused it: `auto-stop` when its auto-stop time came, `idle-stop` when it went `idleStopMinutes` without use, or a rule's reason. A stop someone asked for has none.

autoStopMinutes.description: How long after a start or resume it stops by itself; `null` never.

stopsAt.description: When it will stop by itself, while running; the console's stops-in.

idleStopMinutes.description: How long it may go without use before it stops by itself (`idle-stop`), beside its auto-stop; `null` or absent never. Use is a command (run, followed or killed), and traffic over SSH, the desktop or browser, and its hosted ports. Stopping keeps its disk, as any stop does.

lastActiveAt.description: When it was last used, while running with an idle stop: its start, or its latest use, to within about 20 seconds.

idleStopsAt.description: When its idle stop will stop it if it isn't used before then, while running with one: `lastActiveAt` plus `idleStopMinutes`. It stops within about 30 seconds after, once every gateway's record of use is in.

autoUpgrade.description: An isolate that becomes a microVM by itself when a command needs one (the command's `needsMicrovm`): Kantel upgrades it (`upgradeSandbox`) and runs the command again there, once. Absent: false.

latestSnapshotId.description: The snapshot a resume or fork would use.

latestSnapshotAt.description: When `latestSnapshotId` was taken (its `createdAt`), in milliseconds. Absent from a gateway before it, and where that snapshot's record is gone.

environmentIds.description: Its environments, in order: where two set the same variable, file or repository path, the later one wins. Absent: none.

grants.description: Its own egress grants, on top of its environments'.

mounts.description: Its read-only mounts, as its create named them, each with its status. Absent: none. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`).

hostId.description: The host it runs on (or last ran on): shown to a super-admin, and to anyone who can see the sandbox when it is one of its account's own hosts. Absent until it is placed, and for a shared host to anyone else.

hostReachable.description: Whether the host it is placed on is connected to Kantel now. `false`: it isn't, so Kantel can't reach the sandbox or confirm what its machine is doing, and `state` is its last known state. Calls that need it running (commands, files, ports, SSH, the desktop and browser) answer `unavailable` until the host reconnects; a stop waits a while for it. Answered whether or not `hostId` is shown. Absent until it is placed.

image.description: The base image it is on, by its name in Kantel's base image index: `host` for a microVM (the host images: kernel and root file system), `sandbox` for the container tier.

version.description: The version of the base it is on, such as `host-images-20261104.812`.

outdated.description: Its base isn't the version its channel (`stable`) names now.

security.description: A newer version fixes Critical or High vulnerabilities this one has: restart it on the latest.

SandboxBase.title: SandboxBase
SandboxBase.description: The base image a sandbox's (or a snapshot's) root file system is, and how far behind it is. A running sandbox is never patched underneath: an outdated one stays on its base until it is restarted on the latest (`restartSandboxOnLatest`) or made again. Experimental: present only where the deployment has image patching on (`KANTEL_IMAGE_PATCHING`) and knows the version.

days.description: Whole days since the version after its own was built: how long it has been superseded.

SandboxBaseBehind.title: SandboxBaseBehind
SandboxBaseBehind.description: How far behind its channel it is, while outdated.

SandboxBaseLatest.title: SandboxBaseLatest
SandboxBaseLatest.description: The version its channel names now.

javascript.description: Whether its commands can run JavaScript with `node`: always in a microVM; in an isolate, where its host's isolate runtime has it (each run a fresh V8 isolate, with no npm packages).

python.description: Whether its commands can run Python with `python` (`python3`): always in a microVM; in an isolate, where its host's isolate runtime has it (Pyodide, with the packages it ships, none installed from the internet).

browserSurface.description: Experimental. Whether `openBrowser`'s `url` shows the browser alone rather than the desktop it runs on: the image has a display and a stream for its browser. Absent: false.

pause.description: Whether it can be paused with its memory kept.

SandboxCapabilities.title: SandboxCapabilities
SandboxCapabilities.description: What this sandbox can do, from its type and its host, and for a microVM from what its guest agent found in its image (`guest`): `desktop`, `browser`, `docker` and `kvm` are false where the image lacks them.

environmentGrants.description: Its environments' grants, which it has too.

grants.description: Its own grants, on top of its environments'.

entries.description: Newest first; Kantel keeps the newest 1000.

SandboxEgress.title: SandboxEgress
SandboxEgress.description: A sandbox's egress: what it was made with, its own grants and its log.

pending.description: Its secret files and repositories are set up when the sandbox next runs.

environments.description: In order: where two set the same variable, file or repository path, the later one wins.

SandboxEnvironments.title: SandboxEnvironments
SandboxEnvironments.description: A sandbox's environments, and what each gives it.

variables.description: Its variables a later environment, or the sandbox's own env, sets instead.

files.description: Its secret files' paths a later environment writes instead.

repos.description: Its repositories' paths a later environment clones into instead.

SandboxEnvironmentShadowed.title: SandboxEnvironmentShadowed
SandboxEnvironmentShadowed.description: What of an environment a sandbox doesn't take from it.

SandboxHealth.title: SandboxHealth
SandboxHealth.description: `degraded`: the machine is up but its host can't fully reach it; it keeps running. `unresponsive`: it is running, but its guest agent has stopped answering its host (out of memory, say; its `reason` says why), so its commands and files are refused at once (`sandbox_unresponsive`) rather than left to hang. Recover it (a restart that keeps its disk), or stop and start it; it is `ok` again by itself should its agent answer first.

SandboxMount.title: SandboxMount
SandboxMount.description: A mount of a sandbox's, and whether its files are in place.

stopReason.description: Why it stopped, paused or failed, where Kantel recorded it (the sandbox's `reason`): `auto-stop` when its auto-stop time came, `idle-stop` when it went `idleStopMinutes` without use, a rule's reason when Kantel stopped it, or what failed. A stop someone asked for has none. Not `details.reason`, which is a placement's.

hint.description: What to do, in words, such as `Resume it with kantel resume sbx_4kq9x2mt or POST /v1/sandboxes/sbx_4kq9x2mt/resume, then try again`.

SandboxNotRunning.title: SandboxNotRunning
SandboxNotRunning.description: The `details` of the `conflict` (409) a call that needs a running sandbox (commands, files, ports, file URLs, archives) answers when the sandbox isn't running. A call made while it is starting waits for it, up to 60 seconds, before it answers `sandbox_starting`. Kantel never resumes a stopped sandbox for such a call.

SandboxNotRunningCode.title: SandboxNotRunningCode
SandboxNotRunningCode.description: Why a call that needs a running sandbox was refused. `sandbox_starting`: it was still starting when the call's wait for it ran out; send the call again. `sandbox_stopping`, `sandbox_stopped`, `sandbox_paused`, `sandbox_error`: resume it (`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/resume`), then send the call again. `sandbox_deleting`: it is being deleted. `sandbox_unresponsive`: it is running, but its guest agent doesn't answer (its `health` is `unresponsive`; `stopReason` says why, such as out of memory): recover it (`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/recover`, a restart that keeps its disk), or wait for the agent to answer again.

command.description: Its command line, its arguments joined by spaces (at most 1 KiB of it), or its name in brackets where it has none, as `ps` writes a kernel thread's.

cpuPercent.description: Its CPU over a short sample, as a share of one vCPU in percent: 150 is one and a half.

items.description: By CPU, then memory, most first.

total.description: How many processes the sandbox has.

placeholderPrefix.description: The first 8 characters of its placeholder, such as `kph_7Qx2`.

environmentId.description: The environment whose value it takes.

SandboxProtectedVariable.title: SandboxProtectedVariable
SandboxProtectedVariable.description: A protected variable as one sandbox has it: never its value.

cpu.description: CPU utilisation over the interval ending at `at`, 0 to 1 of the sandbox's own vCPUs.

memUsedBytes.description: Memory in use at `at`. For a microVM, what its guest counts as used (total less available, page cache not counted), so it falls when the guest frees memory; from a host or VM that can't report that, the memory the VM holds on its host, which stays near its high point. For an isolate, its share of its account's runtime.

diskUsedBytes.description: A microVM's own disk in use at `at`, as its guest counts it (df's used). Absent for an isolate, and where the host or the guest's agent doesn't send it.

ioPressure.description: The share of the interval ending at `at` in which at least one of a microVM's tasks waited on IO (its guest kernel's IO pressure, `some`). Absent where the guest has no pressure figures.

oomKills.description: How many processes a microVM's kernel had killed for memory since it booted, at `at`. Absent where its guest's agent doesn't send it or didn't answer in time.

memPressureSome.description: A microVM's memory pressure at `at`: the share of the 10 seconds before it in which at least one of its tasks was stalled waiting for memory (`some` avg10). Absent where the guest has no pressure figures.

memPressureFull.description: As `memPressureSome`, for the share in which every task that wanted to run was stalled (`full` avg10).

vcpus.description: vCPUs: 0 for an isolate, which shares its account's VM's CPU.

SandboxShape.title: SandboxShape
SandboxShape.description: The vCPUs and memory a sandbox asked for: the shape it was made with (a fork, its source's), and once its host places it, what it runs as. Known from the moment it's made, before its host says what it got (`resources`, with its disk). Absent: made by a named size and not yet placed, or made before shapes.

vcpus.description: A microVM's vCPUs. An isolate has none of its own: it shares its account's VM's CPU.

memoryMb.description: Memory in MB. An isolate takes 128 to 512 in steps of 64; a microVM up to what a host offers (`getSandboxShapes`). Needed unless `diskGb` is given alone.

diskGb.description: A microVM's disk in GB, chosen apart from its vCPUs and memory, within `getSandboxShapes`' `microvm.diskGb`. Alone (with `size` or neither), the vCPUs and memory are that size's or the default's. Default: the disk its host gives the shape. Not for an isolate, or with `from`: a sandbox made from a snapshot keeps the snapshot's disk.

SandboxShapeInput.title: SandboxShapeInput
SandboxShapeInput.description: What a new sandbox gets. A microVM restores a template snapshot on its host: by default the one its host keeps for its vCPU count, whatever its memory and disk, so a shape off the presets is as fast as a preset once that count's template is made. A host with shared templates turned off keeps one per preset, and a shape off the presets boots from scratch.

SandboxShapes.title: SandboxShapes
SandboxShapes.description: What a new sandbox in the account may be: the ranges its hosts offer, their presets and the rates.

SandboxSizeName.title: SandboxSizeName
SandboxSizeName.description: A microVM's named size; a deployment may offer fewer. Isolates have none. Superseded by `resources` on create: a named size is still taken for now, alone or with a disk of its own (`resources` with only `diskGb`).

sandboxId.description: Set when it was forked from another sandbox.

disk.description: How its disk was made: `reflink`, a clone of the snapshot's disk that shares its blocks (at once, on a host whose disk is XFS or btrfs); `copy`, a full copy of the snapshot's data (a host on ext4, which has no reflinks); `move`, a live fork's own snapshot's disk; `new`, an empty disk. Absent when it kept its own (a resume).

snapshotMs.description: For a fork of a running sandbox: the live snapshot of its source it was made from.

bootMs.description: Its machine booted, or its snapshot loaded into it (a restore with memory), in milliseconds.

agentMs.description: From then until its guest agent answered, in milliseconds: on a cold boot, the guest's kernel and init too.

hostMs.description: The whole start on its host, in milliseconds: these phases and the rest (its network, identity and mounts).

totalMs.description: From Kantel's call to its host until the host answered, in milliseconds. Well over `hostMs` is time on the way to and from the host, not on it.

SandboxStartup.title: SandboxStartup
SandboxStartup.description: How its machine's latest start (a create, fork, start or resume) took its time, phase by phase, as its host measured it: a slow disk phase is a full copy of its disk, a slow boot or agent phase a busy host. microVMs only, and only from a host that reports it.

SandboxState.title: SandboxState
SandboxState.description: `starting`: being placed and booted. `running`: commands run now. `stopping`: its disk is being saved. `stopped`: no machine; its disk is kept as its newest snapshot, and running programs are gone. `paused`: like `stopped`, but its memory is kept too, so `resume` carries on where it left off (microVMs only). `error`: the last operation failed or the machine was lost; `recover` or `resume` it. `deleting`, `deleted`: erased for good, with its snapshots.

version.description: The template's version it was made from.

snapshotId.description: The template snapshot it started from, `tsn_…`; absent for a fresh boot.

start.description: `snapshot`: it started from the template's built snapshot. `boot`: none was ready, so it booted the template's image and ran its setup itself (a custom image: the one its build made).

SandboxTemplate.title: SandboxTemplate
SandboxTemplate.description: The template a sandbox was made from.

SandboxType.title: SandboxType
SandboxType.description: `isolate`: a V8 isolate running just-bash, a bash written in TypeScript, over files kept in `/workspace`. Starts in milliseconds and costs almost nothing. It has curl, jq, grep, rg, sed, awk and the usual text tools, and `node` (JavaScript and TypeScript, no npm packages) and `python` (Pyodide: the standard library and numpy, no pip install) where its `capabilities` say so (`javascript`, `python`), but no git, package manager or other program of its own, no Docker, desktop, ports or SSH. It can be upgraded to a microVM in place. `microvm`: a Firecracker microVM with a full Linux, root, Docker and `/dev/kvm` inside, a desktop, a browser and SSH.

SandboxUpgrade.title: SandboxUpgrade
SandboxUpgrade.description: A microVM that was an isolate until `at`, when it was upgraded with its ID, files and settings.

memLimitBytes.description: The memory it may use, when its host reports it or its size sets it.

diskTotalBytes.description: Its own disk's size, as its guest counts it, when its host sends disk figures.

peakMemoryBytes.description: The most memory it has used in one reading since it was made (5 s apart from a current host), kept after the readings themselves are gone and after it is deleted. Absent until a reading is kept.

peakCpu.description: Its highest CPU utilisation in one reading since it was made, 0 to 1 of its own vCPUs.

cpuMax.description: The highest CPU reading in the interval, where `measured`. From a mean kept before peaks were, its mean.

memoryMbMax.description: The most memory in use in one reading in the interval, where `measured`: a sandbox's peak can be twice its mean or more, so size it from this. From a mean kept before peaks were, its mean.

measured.description: Whether any kept reading covers the interval: false where there is none (stopped, or older than the week kept), and `cpu` and `memoryMb` are then 0 for want of a figure, not measured as 0. Absent from a gateway before it.

diskUsedBytes.description: The sandbox's own disk in use, its mean over the interval; absent where its host doesn't send it.

ioPressure.description: The share of the interval in which at least one of its tasks waited on IO, its mean; absent where its guest has no pressure figures.

SandboxUsagePoint.title: SandboxUsagePoint
SandboxUsagePoint.description: One interval's means, and its highest CPU and memory. A sandbox keeps a day of 5-minute means and hourly ones for the six days before, so an interval within the day can be as fine as 5 minutes, and one before it is an hour's mean at best.

intervalMs.description: How far apart the points are: 5000 from a host that sends its readings, longer from one that doesn't yet.

points.description: Oldest first, at most the last hour; with `since`, only those after it.

SandboxUsageSeries.title: SandboxUsageSeries
SandboxUsageSeries.description: The sandbox's readings as they came, for a live graph: poll with `since` set to the last point's `at` for only the newer ones.

SandboxVisibility.title: SandboxVisibility
SandboxVisibility.description: `private`: only the person who made it (and API keys of theirs) may see or use it. `organisation`: every member of its organisation may. A personal account's sandboxes are always `private`.

sandboxId.description: The sandbox to save, running or stopped.

snapshotId.description: Save this snapshot of the sandbox's history. Default: its state now.

labels.description: Your own key-value pairs (at most 20, values up to 500 characters), such as `git.base` for the commit a checkout in it is at. Kantel keeps them as given.

replace.description: Replace a saved snapshot of the same name.

minMemoryMb.description: The least memory, in MB, a sandbox made or forked from this snapshot may have, such as 16384 for a monorepo whose type-check needs 13 GB: a create or fork asking for less, by size or `resources`, is refused (`invalid`) before anything is made. A microVM's only. Default: a replace keeps the least of the snapshot it replaces, else none; 0 is none.

memory.description: Saving a running microVM: keep its memory as well as its disk, so a sandbox made from the snapshot carries on where it left off instead of booting, on the same machine size only. Default false: the disk alone, which is several GB smaller and makes sandboxes of any size. A stopped sandbox or a snapshot of its history is saved as that snapshot is.

content.description: At most 1 MiB, in `encoding`. Required for a new file; left out, the file keeps its contents.

SetEnvironmentFileBody.title: SetEnvironmentFileBody
SetEnvironmentFileBody.description: `encoding` says how `content` is written: `utf8` (the default) or `base64`.

value.description: Required for a new variable and when it becomes protected or plain. Left out on a protected one, it keeps its value (to change its bindings); a new value for a protected one is a rotation.

bindings.description: A protected variable's destinations, at least one. Left out, a protected one keeps its own.

publicUrl.description: An http(s) origin, such as `https://kantel.example.com`; `null` goes back to the deployment's own.

diskGb.description: The disk the host gives a fresh sandbox of this size. One made from a snapshot keeps that snapshot's disk.

ShapeRates.title: ShapeRates
ShapeRates.description: What an hour costs, per vCPU and GB; absent where it is free.

name.description: A saved snapshot's name, unique in its account.

labels.description: Your own key-value pairs (at most 20, values up to 500 characters), such as `git.base` for the commit a checkout in it is at. Kantel keeps them as given.

sandboxId.description: The sandbox it was taken of; absent once that is deleted.

memory.description: Whether it holds the sandbox's memory as well as its disk (a pause).

minMemoryMb.description: A saved microVM snapshot's least memory, in MB, as its save gave it (`SaveSnapshotBody.minMemoryMb`): a create or fork from it with less is refused (`invalid`) before anything is made, rather than started on a machine its work can't run in. Absent: any.

sizeBytes.description: The space it takes on its host's disk now, kept up to date from what the host measures: the blocks its files have allocated, each file linked into several snapshots counted once, for one of them (a saved snapshot before an automatic one, then the oldest). So a saved snapshot kept from a sandbox's history counts the files it shares with its source, and its source only what is its own; a size can change when a snapshot it shares files with is deleted. A copy that shares disk blocks without sharing the file (a reflinked copy) counts in full. Memory not yet written to the disk counts nothing. Absent while it is unknown.

uses.description: How many sandboxes were made or forked from it, deleted ones included. Absent from a gateway before it.

takenAt.description: When the state it holds was taken, in milliseconds. `createdAt` (when it was taken or saved), except for a saved snapshot copied from an earlier one (a stopped sandbox's newest, or `snapshotId` from its history), which keeps that one's time. Absent for a saved snapshot from before this was kept.

SnapshotKind.title: SnapshotKind
SnapshotKind.description: `automatic`: one of a sandbox's own history, taken as it runs and at each stop; the newest is what a resume or fork uses, and older ones expire. `saved`: kept under a name until deleted, and usable as a template for new sandboxes, even after its sandbox is deleted.

user.description: Names the sandbox to the gateway.

command.description: A command line that connects, such as `ssh -p 2222 sbx_4kq9x2mt@ssh.example`.

proxyUrl.description: When there is no SSH gateway to dial: a WebSocket URL carrying the sandbox's SSH as binary frames, for an `ssh -o ProxyCommand=…` (`kantel ssh-proxy` is one). Anyone holding it can start a connection until `expiresAt`.

privateKey.description: When Kantel made the key pair: its private key, shown once.

publicKey.description: An OpenSSH public key to let in. Absent: Kantel makes a key pair for this access.

ttlMinutes.description: How long a connection can be started with this access; one started in time stays open. Default 10.

clientName.description: What is signing in, shown to the person who approves it and given to its key: `kantel on build-01`.

personal.description: Ask for a personal access token, which acts in every account its approver belongs to, rather than an API key in one account. Default false, for a device from before personal tokens.

keepMemory.description: Pause instead: keep its memory as well as its disk (`paused`). microVMs only. Default false.

labels.description: Your own key-value pairs (at most 20, values up to 500 characters), such as `git.base` for the commit a checkout in it is at. Kantel keeps them as given.

memory.description: Keep the running microVM's memory as well as its disk, so a sandbox made from the snapshot carries on where it left off instead of booting, on the same machine size only. Default false: the disk alone, which is several GB smaller and makes sandboxes of any size.

endpoint.description: An OTLP/HTTP collector's base URL; `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/logs` are added.

headerNames.description: The headers sent with each export; values never shown.

TelemetryExport.title: TelemetryExport
TelemetryExport.description: Where an account's telemetry goes: sandbox metrics (`kantel.sandbox.cpu`, `kantel.sandbox.memory_bytes` and `kantel.sandbox.running_seconds`) every 60 seconds, and each lifecycle event as an OTLP log record when it happens.

TelemetryTestResult.title: TelemetryTestResult
TelemetryTestResult.description: What the collector answered to an empty export sent on save.

version.description: Its current version; a new spec makes the next.

sandboxCount.description: How many sandboxes were made from it and still exist.

Template.title: Template
Template.description: A microVM profile: image, base, resources, variables, setup and egress, versioned.

TemplateBase.title: TemplateBase
TemplateBase.description: The Kantel base image it boots: a channel the deployment publishes (`/v1/template-bases`), or a digest one published. Default: `kantel/sandbox`'s `stable` channel; until that channel publishes a digest, each host's own sandbox image.

history.description: Every digest it has published, newest first.

TemplateBaseChannel.title: TemplateBaseChannel
TemplateBaseChannel.description: A base image's channel and the digests it has published.

TemplateBaseChannelRef.title: TemplateBaseChannelRef
TemplateBaseChannelRef.description: Follow a channel: rebuilt when it publishes a new digest.

TemplateBasePinned.title: TemplateBasePinned
TemplateBasePinned.description: Pin an exact digest, one its channels published: never rebuilt for a new release.

releases.description: How many digests the base's channel has published since the pinned one.

TemplateBehind.title: TemplateBehind
TemplateBehind.description: How far a pinned base is behind its channel.

state.description: `none`: nothing built yet; sandboxes boot fresh. `stale`: what is built is for an older key, and used until its replacement is ready if it is of the template's current version. A `ready` snapshot of an older version starts no sandbox: they boot fresh until the current version's is ready. A template with a Dockerfile or image reference doesn't boot fresh before its current version's image is built: its sandboxes wait for that build (`unavailable` until then).

channel.description: The channel it followed; absent when pinned.

baseDigest.description: Empty while the channel has no published digest.

imageDigest.description: The digest of the image its host booted, as the host reported it: for an `image`, the digest the reference resolved to; for a `dockerfile`, the built image's ID.

source.description: The template image's kind it was built from. Absent: `kantel-base`.

dockerfileDigest.description: For a `dockerfile`, the SHA-256 of the Dockerfile built, `sha256:…`.

TemplateBuiltFrom.title: TemplateBuiltFrom
TemplateBuiltFrom.description: What a template snapshot was built from.

source.description: A custom image's source: `dockerfile:sha256:…` (the Dockerfile's digest) or `image:<ref>`. Absent for `kantel-base`.

imageDigest.description: A custom image's digest: the one an `image` pins from the start, else the one its build made or resolved, recorded once the build answers. Absent for `kantel-base`.

memoryMb.description: With `vcpus`, the machine it was built as: the template's resources, which a fresh boot from it gets too.

TemplateCacheKey.title: TemplateCacheKey
TemplateCacheKey.description: What a template snapshot is for: a change to any part builds another. A create starts from it only when it gets the same vCPUs and memory.

dockerfile.description: A Dockerfile, built with no build context. `ARG KANTEL_BASE` then `FROM $KANTEL_BASE` starts from the template's `base`; any other `FROM` image is pulled.

TemplateDockerfileImage.title: TemplateDockerfileImage
TemplateDockerfileImage.description: Built in an isolated build microVM whose only way out is the sandbox egress proxy: its pulls, `RUN` steps and remote `ADD`s reach the template's egress grants and the registries the host's operator allows, and never a host, private or metadata address.

TemplateImage.title: TemplateImage
TemplateImage.description: What a template's machines boot: `kantel-base`, Kantel's base image customised by the setup script; a `dockerfile`; or an `image` reference. Custom images are built only on hosts that build them in a build microVM. Default: `kantel-base`.

ref.description: An image reference, such as `python:3.13-slim` or `ghcr.io/acme/ci@sha256:…`. A tag is resolved when the template is built, and again on a rebuild.

TemplateImageRef.title: TemplateImageRef
TemplateImageRef.description: Pulled in an isolated build microVM, as a Dockerfile's images are. The template's `base` isn't used. An image that isn't one of Kantel's boots through the guest agent the host injects.

TemplateKantelBaseImage.title: TemplateKantelBaseImage
TemplateKantelBaseImage.description: The template's `base` itself, as its deployment publishes it; the setup script adds the rest.

TemplateNetwork.title: TemplateNetwork
TemplateNetwork.description: Egress grants for its sandboxes and for its build's boot.

TemplateResources.title: TemplateResources
TemplateResources.description: Its sandboxes' and its builds' vCPUs and memory, exactly, unless a create names a size; a deployment must offer a size with at least them. Default 2 vCPUs and 4096 MB.

keyHash.description: The SHA-256 hex of the key's canonical JSON.

hostId.description: The host it was built on, which holds it.

TemplateSnapshot.title: TemplateSnapshot
TemplateSnapshot.description: A built template: its image booted once, its setup run, then snapshotted. A cache entry Kantel throws away and rebuilds at will, never one of the account's snapshots.

TemplateSnapshotState.title: TemplateSnapshotState
TemplateSnapshotState.description: `stale`: built for a key no longer wanted, and used while its replacement builds only if it is of the template's current version. `failed`: not tried again until its key changes or the template is rebuilt. `discarded`: thrown away.

env.description: Plain variables, not secrets: under the environment's and the create's own.

setup.description: A shell script run once, as root, when the snapshot is built (or at a fresh boot).

TemplateSpec.title: TemplateSpec
TemplateSpec.description: A template version's definition, never changed once made. Answered with every default filled in.

draining.description: Stop placing new sandboxes on it.

savedSnapshotBytesLimit.description: The most bytes of saved snapshots each account may keep on this host (`Host.savedSnapshotBytesLimit`); `null` removes the limit.

idleStopMinutes.description: Its idle stop; `null` turns it off. A running sandbox's idle time counts from now.

extendMinutes.description: Move `stopsAt` to this long from now.

autoUpgrade.description: Turns its `autoUpgrade` on or off: an isolate that becomes a microVM by itself when its runtime says a command needs one, and runs the whole command again there. Once on, any caller that may run commands in it may cause the upgrade.

UpdateTemplateBody.title: UpdateTemplateBody
UpdateTemplateBody.description: A `spec` that differs from the current one makes a new version.

image.description: The microVM's base image. Default: the deployment's.

wait.description: Answer once the microVM runs with the isolate's files (the default), or `false` as soon as the upgrade has begun (`starting`). Either way a failed upgrade leaves the isolate as it was.

UpgradeSandboxBody.title: UpgradeSandboxBody
UpgradeSandboxBody.description: The microVM to make: `size` or `resources`, and `image`, as a create takes them. Every field is optional: `{}` makes the deployment's default microVM.

recentCpu.description: CPU utilisation, 0 to 1, over the last 24 intervals of 5 minutes, oldest first. The last may be the interval under way.

recentMemory.description: Memory in use, in bytes, over the same intervals as `recentCpu` (the same length), oldest first.

UsageSparklines.title: UsageSparklines
UsageSparklines.description: A host's recent CPU and memory, for sparklines.

recentCpu.description: CPU utilisation, 0 to 1, over the last 24 intervals of 5 minutes, oldest first: a sparkline. The last may be the interval under way.

recentMemory.description: Memory in use, in bytes, over the same intervals as `recentCpu` (the same length), oldest first.

peakMemoryBytes.description: The most memory it has used in one reading since it was made (5 s apart from a current host), kept after the readings themselves are gone and after it is deleted. Absent until a reading is kept.

peakCpu.description: Its highest CPU utilisation in one reading since it was made, 0 to 1 of its own vCPUs.

viewOnly.description: Watch only: no keyboard or mouse. Default false.

ttlMinutes.description: How long the URLs can be opened for; a view or connection opened in time stays open. Default 10.

Webhook.title: Webhook
Webhook.description: An HTTPS endpoint that gets an account's events, signed as Standard Webhooks are: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body`, keyed by the secret after its `whsec_`). Failed deliveries are retried with backoff, up to 8 attempts.
